source.title: A Unified Noise-Curvature View of Loss of Trainability
source.authors: Gunbir Singh Baveja; Alex Lewandowski; Mark Schmidt

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests loss of trainability in continual learning on random-label MNIST, a new setting relative to the claim’s benchmark training-error results; its task-accuracy measure does not test the listed versions’ specific outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study reports task-accuracy outcomes and diagnoses loss of trainability in a 40-task random-label MNIST stream. These results do not measure training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or test the specific conditions in V1–V6; cited prior-work results and unquantified figure values are not extracted as separate results.
record.test_reason: The study measures continual-learning trainability and scheduler performance in an Adam-trained MLP on random-label MNIST. It does not test any specified version: there is no convolutional training-error experiment, teacher–student width comparison, depth or initialization comparison, stability-threshold recovery experiment, or controlled batch-normalization speed comparison. Its adaptive noise thresholds are different from V5's initial linearized-model stability limit and edge-of-stability dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they argue that complementary gradient-noise and curvature-volatility signals diagnose loss of trainability better than individual indicators, and report improved maintained task accuracy with their per-layer scheduler across CReLU, L2 and Wasserstein baselines. This is a proposed diagnostic account, rather than an established complete explanation; the plotted prediction proxy is scaled to the observed accuracy range. Appendix A.2 also states that CReLU single-signal schedulers eventually attain higher accuracy than the combined method despite initial instability.
record.recipe_differences: Continual learning on sequential random-label MNIST tasks with a two-layer MLP and Adam; the study examines adaptive step-size scheduling and task accuracy rather than benchmark training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by baseline method: vanilla CReLU and L2 decay to near-random accuracy, while Wasserstein regularization has mild decay; the scheduler improves or stabilizes task accuracy across the three.

fits_no_version.finding: Across random-label MNIST tasks, vanilla CReLU stays near chance, vanilla L2 deteriorates toward chance, and Wasserstein regularization shows milder decay; the proposed per-layer scheduler improves or stabilizes task accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive per-layer step-size control can mitigate loss of trainability in the tested continual-learning MLP configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 gives configurations where Hessian rank, unit-sign entropy, sharpness, weight norms, gradient norms, or gradient-to-parameter ratios fail individually to predict task-accuracy deterioration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual optimization indicators do not consistently predict continual-learning trainability across the tested configurations.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2025: 17th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning; arXiv preprint
record.problems: The experiments use a two-layer MLP on random-label MNIST rather than the listed benchmark architectures and datasets. Runs are averaged over 3 seeds, but no uncertainty estimates are stated in the supplied text. The main task-accuracy comparisons are shown in figures without exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only numerical values and cited prior-work results were not extracted. The appendix also reports additional scheduler ablations, task-length comparisons, and per-layer versus full-network controller comparisons; these concern scheduler performance or internal indicators and do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and the stated size, stopping and regularization qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher–student problems.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated plain-tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal/gradient propagation, training speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.

Above-threshold loss recovery, curvature reduction, divergence boundaries, and full-batch sharpness tracking the stability threshold. Adam noise-bound violations and task-accuracy decline do not establish these dynamics.

Accuracy gain speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and comparable normalization-free residual training with Fixup. BatchNorm's trainability failure in Figure 1 lacks the required controlled comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No version-specific verdicts are warranted. The main exclusion is the mismatch in systems, comparisons and outcomes, rather than a demonstrated distinction between task accuracy and training accuracy. All runs are averaged over three seeds; exact main-result values and uncertainty estimates are not supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, and the stated model-size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and width relative to teacher size.
Depth effects, plain versus residual shortcuts, and the stated ImageNet/CIFAR-10 settings.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability limit, loss recovery, and sharpness behavior in the stated settings.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup’s normalization-free residual training results.

rows.subject: two-layer MLP (width 256), vanilla CReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a sequence of random-label MNIST tasks without the proposed scheduler.
rows.value: Vanilla and reset stay near random accuracy.
rows.note: Task accuracy in continual learning, not training classification error on the current task.
rows.check: The reported near-random task accuracy is supported, but cannot establish an effect in V1–V6. The value combines vanilla and reset conditions although the subject names only vanilla; separate them. The note categorically excluding current-task training accuracy is unsupported: the experiment uses MNIST training images for random-label memorization, without clearly defining a separate evaluation split.
